newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, May 29.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, May 29.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 ended with modest losses, as concerns about the fate of EMU in the wake of the Bundesbank row with Bonn and worries about the outcome of the French elections were softened by a late advance in the U.S. bond market. The blue chip share index ended 5.2 points lower at 4,672.3, though advancers led decliners 56 to 42.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended IBIS computer dealings, drawing strength from a firmer dollar and shrugging off the clash between the Bundesbank and Bonn over plans to revalue the country's gold. The IBIS DAX, which reflects computer trade in the 30-share index, ended up 8.78 points at 3,635.38 points, or slightly down from the DAX's bourse close on Wednesday at 3,636.42. Bourse trading was closed on Thursday due to a regional holiday but the IBIS computer system was open.

PARIS - The bourse closed with narrow losses, after losing early gains in a busy session marked by conflicting rumours over private opinion polls on Sunday's parliamentary runoff vote. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 3.93 points or 0.15 percent at 2,579.24.

ZURICH - Shares closed little changed after a volatile session marked by the tendency of Swiss stocks to fluctuate in line with moves in other markets. The SMI index of leading shares closed 1.0 lower at 5,132.1 and the all-share SPI was down 1.59 points to 3,248.80. The turnover leader on the day was UBS, which rose 26 francs to end at 1,571.

TOKYO - Stocks closed slightly lower due to profit-taking after the previous day's sharp advance in the key average by more than three percent. Brokers said investors were prompted to secure temporary profits as the dollar briefly dipped below 116.00 yen. The 225-share Nikkei average lost 39.11 points or 0.19 percent to finish at 20,312.23. June Nikkei futures fell 90 points to 20,310.

HONG KONG - Blue chips took a beating, cast out of the limelight by the long-awaited debut of red chip newcomer Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd, which tripled in price on its first trading day. The Hang Seng blue-chip index slid 139.91 points, or 0.96 percent, to 14,416.57 after tumbling to a low of 14,299.01.

SYDNEY - Shares captured light gains by the close, collecting yet another record high and record closing level on the way. The All Ordinaries index climbed 5.4 points to 2,590.6, having touched a record high of 2,591.5, surpassing the previous record high of 2,590.4 reached on Wednesday.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended strongly, bouyed by hopes of an early interest rate cut after a worse-than-expected first quarter gross domestic product growth. The all-share index gained 33.9 points to 7,074.7 points, the industrial index added 36.0 points to 8,317.9 points and the gold index rose 2.8 points to 1,181.3 points.
